statements.text: Our committee realizes military competition in the 21st century will be decided by our willingness to harness emerging technology. [...] This NDAA accelerates the development of artificial intelligence, offensive cyber, hypersonics, and unmanned platforms.
statements.context: Senate floor remarks by Senator Roger Wicker summarizing the FY2024 National Defense Authorization Act after its passage.

statements.text: AI technologies hold incredible potential for the future of our country, and it is important for Congress to provide guidance to industry as new applications emerge. https://t.co/6LvKwBPbB9

China and Russia are vying to win the race for dominance of 21st-century military technologies. Through AI, hypersonics, and unmanned system investments, Republicans are keeping the U.S. military ahead of our adversaries in the #FY24NDAA. https://t.co/KiMkbRXW1s

Fundamentally, the rule places burdensome constraints on U.S. companies that would be difficult to comply with and even harder for the Federal government to enforce. Buyers, particularly in Tier 2 countries that are constrained from purchasing U.S. technology, would be incentivized to turn to Communist China’s unregulated, cheap substitutes.
statements.venue: Letter to Commerce Secretary Lutnick (with Sen. Ricketts) on the AI Diffusion Rule, posted on Wicker's website

statements.text: I applaud the Trump administration for rescinding the Biden-era AI diffusion rule, which would have hurt America's competitiveness in the global AI race. Replacing the rule with a simpler, more targeted framework will protect American innovation and disrupt efforts by China to advance their AI capabilities. This is a direct threat to our national security, and I am pleased the Trump administration recognizes this urgency. https://t.co/5880zrI50X

The U.S. must lead in AI innovation and accountability. Today, President Trump signed the Take It Down Act. This new law protects people from AI deepfakes which often target families and children. Read more about how the world is adapting to AI.https://t.co/3w0RGPUf1B
Americans recognize that AI has nearly unlimited potential to benefit humanity. But the technology also raises difficult questions about privacy and job security.
statements.venue: Wicker weekly column/press release, 'Senator Wicker Helping Maintain America's AI Edge'

statements.text: Simply put, if we do not win the AI race, China will – directly threatening our national security.
statements.venue: Wicker weekly column/press release, 'Senator Wicker Helping Maintain America's AI Edge'

statements.text: Any government regulations on AI must begin with a “light touch” so that innovators can experiment, prototype, and compete. In this way, we mirror the approach the government took with the internet, allowing that technology to grow and develop in the United States.
statements.venue: Wicker weekly column/press release, 'Senator Wicker Helping Maintain America's AI Edge'

statements.text: Congress passed and President Trump signed into law a bill called the Take It Down Act. A key part of that law sets punishments for those who use AI to create certain pornographic deepfakes.
statements.venue: Wicker weekly column/press release, 'Senator Wicker Helping Maintain America's AI Edge'

statements.text: Today, President Donald J. Trump signed the TAKE IT DOWN Act into law — a key initiative of First Lady Melania Trump and a landmark step in the fight to protect victims of digital exploitation.
statements.context: White House release compiling statements from lawmakers and officials on the signing of the TAKE IT DOWN Act.

statements.text: Artificial intelligence capabilities continue to expand and become part of daily life. Federal courts have begun using this technology to improve their processes. This legislation would examine the legal, technical, and constitutional implications of AI in the U.S. judicial system. Ensuring accuracy is critical to fair justice.
statements.venue: Statement on the Research and Oversight of AI in Courts Act of 2026, quoted by MeriTalk

statements.text:
I appreciate President Trump’s statement on Anthropic following @SusieWiles' meeting with the company about their new model, Claude Mythos. 

Anthropic has made this model available to the U.S. government ahead of public release. The President is absolutely right. AI is evolving too fast and is too important for us not to work together.

I know the President intends to discuss trade and AI with the Chinese leadership—and rightfully so. Perhaps some progress will be made. But, during every minute of dialogue, our commander-in-chief should keep in mind that his guest is a brutal, unelected, and oppressive dictator who seeks to dominate his neighbors and whose military arsenal is aimed directly at the United States of America.

The United States must win the AI race. This will take close coordination with industry, neighborhoods, and local leaders. Mississippi families and taxpayers should not be left funding data center construction. Today, I voted to advance the Ratepayer Protection Act. The bill would set standards that states can consider to make data center owners responsible for any extra energy costs. The bill passed the House of Representatives 417 to 3, but nearly every Senate Democrat voted no. They blocked a widely supported solution, opting to put partisan politics over Americans’ pocketbooks.

America must beat China in the artificial intelligence race, and we can do so without letting data centers harm our communities. Recent surveys have found Americans increasingly worried about data centers, which power AI’s immense processing requirements. Data centers are essential to our 21st century economy, but we can prevent these new facilities from raising our utility bills, disrupting the water supply, or spoiling neighborhood beauty.
statements.venue: Wicker op-ed/weekly column 'Wicker touts data center benefits'

statements.text: The fact is this: The nation that wins in AI will lead the 21st century. Yet without data centers, the United States won’t stand a chance at victory. In any technological leap, our government must ensure the community is protected, and we must lead in innovation.
statements.venue: Wicker op-ed/weekly column 'Wicker touts data center benefits'
